styleExamples.title: Tattoo style guide
styleExamples.subtitle: An iconic example per style — tap one to use it.

styleDescriptions.line-art: Bold, continuous outlines with little or no shading.
styleDescriptions.minimalist: Sparse, essential shapes — only what's necessary.
styleDescriptions.geometric: Precise shapes, symmetry and repeating patterns.
styleDescriptions.traditional: Bold lines, limited colours, classic Americana.
styleDescriptions.neo-traditional: Traditional with richer detail and a wider palette.
styleDescriptions.blackwork: Dense solid-black fills with high contrast.
styleDescriptions.dotwork: Shading built from many tiny dots — stippling.
styleDescriptions.tribal: Bold black silhouettes inspired by ancient motifs.
styleDescriptions.watercolor: Loose washes of colour with soft, painted edges.
styleDescriptions.japanese: Irezumi: waves, koi, dragons and bold linework.
styleDescriptions.new-school: Cartoonish, exaggerated forms and bright colours.
styleDescriptions.sketch: Hand-drawn pencil look with visible strokes.
styleDescriptions.engraving: Etching-style hatching, like an old print.
styleDescriptions.biomechanical: Mechanical parts woven into flesh and bone.
styleDescriptions.trash-polka: Red-and-black collage of brushstrokes and text.
